investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-08-13T12:32–12:39Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod ever reached a running state, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing a complete contract validation failure.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that label. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for peer-pod VMs at the time of the eval run. Preemption was also exhausted ("No preemption victims found"), meaning no lower-priority pods could be evicted to free capacity. The failure is localized to the remote-agent VM provisioning layer in the production-api environment; this is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity signal, not a confirmed user-traffic outage.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: all existing remote-agent VM slots are occupied by live or leaked pods, leaving zero allocatable capacity. Supported by all three scheduler messages reporting 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' with no preemption victims.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch for 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label (e.g. kata.peerpods.io/vm capable) that only 2 nodes carry, so the effective schedulable pool is already constrained to 2 nodes before capacity is considered. If those 2 nodes are fully consumed, the entire cluster is unschedulable for this workload.

TERTIARY — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without being cleaned up: if prior eval runs or user sessions left pods in a non-terminal state, they would consume VM slots without releasing them, accelerating exhaustion.

QUATERNARY — cluster under-provisioning: the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may have an insufficient VM slot quota for the expected concurrent remote-agent load, making exhaustion likely under normal usage.

investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two nodes that carry that label. Preemption was also exhausted ("No preemption victims found"), meaning no lower-priority pods could be evicted to free capacity. The failure is localized to the remote-agent VM provisioning layer in the production-api environment; this is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity signal, not a confirmed user-traffic outage.

investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not run successfully in at least 708 minutes (~11.8 hours). The snapshot file itself is reachable and structurally valid (all required evidence fields are present, source=github-actions, hasLiveSource=true, hasNonUnknownFeatureData=true), but its embedded generation timestamp is too old to satisfy the `snapshotAgeMinutes <= 300` assertion defined in the expected-output contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482. This is an eval-detected workflow scheduling or execution gap, not a website availability outage.
